results.explanation: Accepted policy: note creation requires all three stated global permissions plus object-level change_document authorization; object view alone would not suffice, while an object-level change grant does. The declared handler-entry premise (an assumption, not source or deployment proof) states that this authenticated caller has add_note, view_document, and change_document globally, has object view and change_document grants on the existing document, and is not its owner. Observed behavior: PaperlessNotePermissions requires those three global permissions for POST at src/documents/permissions.py:673-685. The handler binds request.user to currentUser and loads the document identified by pk; its earlier view check is at src/documents/views.py:17-22. For POST, it tests change_document with the owner-aware helper and returns forbidden only if that check fails at src/documents/views.py:37-46. The helper returns true for an unowned object, ownership, or a matching object permission; therefore non-ownership is not conclusive, and the declared object-level change grant satisfies the checker at src/documents/permissions.py:624-635. The forbidden branch is not taken, so execution reaches Note.objects.create at src/documents/views.py:48-52. Thus the accepted policy is satisfied and the source-visible result is allow.

binding.statement: The protected existing document is loaded by the handler from Document objects using the supplied pk and retained as doc.

control.statement: For POST, the note permission class requires add_note, view_document, and change_document global permissions and checks them with request.user.has_perms.
The decisive POST control checks owner-aware change_document authorization on doc and returns forbidden only when that check fails.

effect.statement: After the change_document check passes, the protected effect creates a Note associated with doc and currentUser.

condition.statement: The owner-aware helper authorizes when the document is unowned, owned by the caller, or the object-permission checker confirms the requested permission; consequently a matching object change grant can authorize a non-owner.

citations.quote:
def has_perms_owner_aware(user, perms, obj):
    """
    Legacy slow path (guardian-backed) single-object permission check.

    The queryset-filtering side of this migrated onto
    ``PermittedObjectsFilter``/``permitted_object_ids()``, but this
    single-object check still has many production callers. Several callers
    remain across ``documents/``, ``paperless_mail/``, and ``paperless_ai/``
    -- grep for this function name before removing it.
    """
    checker = ObjectPermissionChecker(user)
    return obj.owner is None or obj.owner == user or checker.has_perm(perms, obj)

condition.statement: Before method-specific POST handling, the handler checks owner-aware view_document authorization on doc and returns forbidden when it fails.

results.explanation: Accepted policy: note creation requires all three stated global permissions plus object-level change_document authorization; an object view grant alone would be insufficient, but document ownership can satisfy the required object control. The declared handler-entry premise (an assumption, not source or deployment proof) states that this authenticated caller has add_note, view_document, and change_document globally and owns the existing document. Observed behavior: PaperlessNotePermissions requires those three global permissions for POST at src/documents/permissions.py:673-685. The handler binds request.user to currentUser and loads the document identified by pk; its earlier view check is at src/documents/views.py:17-22. For POST, it tests change_document with the owner-aware helper and returns forbidden only if that check fails at src/documents/views.py:37-46. The helper treats obj.owner == user as sufficient independently of an explicit object permission at src/documents/permissions.py:624-635. Therefore the unchanged ownership premise satisfies the accepted policy's object-control alternative and the observed owner-aware check. The forbidden branch is not taken, so execution reaches Note.objects.create at src/documents/views.py:48-52. The scenario key does not alter the premise: this is an ownership-authorized case, not a case authorized merely by object view.
